This appeal coming on for admission this day, the court passed the following:
AWARD
With the consent of both the parties, matter is heard finally at motion stage.

1 2.

The appellant has preferred this appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "MV Act") for the enhancement of the compensation amount awarded in Claim Case No.163/2018 passed by the V Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Dewas on 14/08/2019, whereby an amount of Rs.1,49,245/- has been awarded to the appellant towards the compensation.

3. The relevant and necessary facts of the case are that on 21/01/2018 at about 07:45 am appellant was going by his motorcycle towards Dewas from Maksi, when he reached nearby the Navada Phata,
at that time, respondent No.1 by riding his motorcycle bearing registration number MP-41-MY-4721 rashly and negligently came there and dashed the appellant's motorcycle.
As a result of the said accident, appellant fell down on the spot and sustained severe injuries on his right knee and left shoulder as well as on the other parts of the body.

He was admitted in M.G. Hospital, Dewas and thereafter, in Sanskar Hospital and Research Centre, Dewas and spent more than Rs.1,00,000/-
towards his treatment.

entities.text: Sanskar Hospital and Research Centre, Dewas
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He also got permanent disability due to the injury sustained in the accident.
Respondent No.2 was the owner of the said motorcycle and the said motorcycle was insured with the respondent No.3 at the time of accident.

4. Respondent No.2 was remained ex parte before the below Tribunal and respondent No.1 denied all the averments made in the claim petition by submitting that he did not caused any accident and he has been falsely implicated in the claim petition.
However, he is having a valid driving licence and the vehicle was insured with the respondent No.3, therefore, he is not liable for payment of any claim.
5. Respondent No.3 contended that FIR has been lodged on the next day and vehicle number and model number was not mentioned in the documents prepared in the hospital.
Respondent No.1 was not having any valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Entire case is doubtful and due to the breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy, Insurance Company is not liable to pay any claim.

6. Learned below Tribunal after framing the issues, recording and appreciating the evidence available on record, partly allowed the claim petition and passed an award of Rs.1,49,245/- towards compensation with interest @ 6% per annum.
Being aggrieved by the findings given by the below Tribunal, this appeal has been preferred by the appellant.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the below tribunal has committed legal and factual error by not considering the fact that the appellant has sustained 44% permanent disability in his right leg, which is duly proved by the Permanent Disability Certificate (Ex.-P/44) issued by the Dr. I.
K. Shaikh.

The appellant was working as a Electrician and was earning Rs.14,547/- per month as salary, but the same was not considered by the below Tribunal and not awarded any amount in the head of the medical expenses, attendant, transportation, special diet and loss of wages.
Hence, he prays for enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the below Tribunal.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.3 opposes the prayer and prays for its rejection by submitting that impugned order passed by the below Tribunal is just, proper and adequate and Manish vs Jeevan on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15290165/
2 not deserve for any interference.

9. Despite service of notice, nobody appears on behalf of the respondents No.1 and 2.
10.
I have heard arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire record with due care.

11. It is established from the oral as well as documentary evidence available on record that the accident took place by the offending vehicle being driven by the respondent No.1 and at the time of accident, the offending vehicle was duly insured with the respondent No.3 Insurance Company.
There is no material on record to show that there was any breach of insurance policy by the owner or driver of the offending vehicle.
12. The moot question to be addressed in the appeal preferred by the appellant is, as to whether the Tribunal was justified in awarding an amount of Rs.1,49,245/- to the appellant.
The appellant Manish deposed before the below Tribunal that he sustained grievous injury on the right knee and left shoulder and his tibia fibula bone has been fractured.

He remain admitted in District Hospital,
Dewas and spent more than Rs.1,50,000/- towards his treatment.
The papers of the treatment are Ex.-P/13 to P/39.
At the time of accident, he was working in Innovsource Services Pvt. Ltd. and was getting salary of Rs.15,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, he could not attend his services from 27/01/2018 to 18/06/2018.
The relevant certificates are Ex.-P/40 to P/42.
The statement of the appellant is well supported by Dr. I. K. Sheikh (PW-2), who opined that the appellant has sustained 27% permanent disability and his disability certificate is Ex.-P/44.
Respondent No.3 did not examine any witness before the trial Court in its rebuttal, therefore, there is no reason to disbelieve the statements of appellant Manish and Dr. I. K. Sheikh.
13. On the basis of the statements of appellant Manish and Dr. I. K. Sheikh, it is proved that appellant sustained permanent disability.

Although his income was shown Rs.15,000/- per month,
but the appellant did not examine his employer.

In absence of examining the material witness regarding the salary of the appellant, it is not proved that he was earning salary of Rs.15,000/- per month, but as per chart of the year 2018 containing guidelines / instructions issued by the M. P.
State Legal Services Authority, which is based upon the income chart endorsed by the Labour Department, Govt. of M. P., the wages of an unskilled labour may be considered as Rs.7,000/- per month.

sentences.text: 14. This Court has carefully perused the impugned award and found that the Tribunal has discussed the factual as well as evidential aspects in the impugned award and awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,49,245/- by taking into account the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.5,925/-.

The below Tribunal has assessed the loss of 5% in future income, which come to Rs.3,555/- per annum and has applied multiplier of 17 as per the evidence came on record and the age of the appellant at the time of accident, therefore, the appellant has been awarded loss of future income Rs.60,435/-.

Besides,
the below Tribunal has also awarded Rs.66,960/- towards medical expenses, Rs.10,000/- towards attainder, transport and special diet and Rs.11,85/- towards loss of wages.

Looking to the age and income of the appellant, the amount of compensation awarded under various heads appears to be on Manish vs Jeevan on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15290165/
3 lower side.
15.

In the considered opinion of this Court, it would be just and proper to award a further lump sum amount of Rs.1,00,000/- in all heads over and above the amount of compensation, which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.1,00,000/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
16. In view of the above, the appeal is partly allowed and the appellant is entitled to the total compensation of Rs.2,49,245/-, whereas the below tribunal has awarded only a sum of Rs.1,49,245/-.
Hence, the appellant is entitled for enhancement of Rs.1,00,000/-.
The enhanced amount will bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the tribunal and will be governed by the same conditions as contained in the award of the tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
